tests.title: Oblong spacer block (plan 1)
tests.brief: A 3D-printed PLA spacer block. The base is a 40 mm by 25 mm plate 5 mm thick. A 10 mm diameter post 8 mm tall stands in the middle of it, with a 1.5 mm fillet where the post meets the plate. A 4 mm hole runs all the way through the post and the plate. Two 3 mm mounting holes pass all the way through the plate, 30 mm apart. It must weigh no more than 10 g. It carries no load - it is a printed spacer, so there is no load case.

tests.title: Stainless collar, one set screw (plan 2)
tests.brief: A stainless steel shaft collar. The outer diameter is 30 mm and it is 12 mm long. A 16 mm bore runs all the way through on the axis. One 5 mm set screw hole passes through the wall from the outside into the bore, halfway along the length. It carries no load - it is a locating collar, so there is no load case.

tests.title: Flange disc, two bolt holes (plan 3)
tests.brief: A steel flange disc 60 mm across and 8 mm thick. A 20 mm bore runs all the way through the centre. Two 6 mm bolt holes pass all the way through the disc, 40 mm apart. It carries no load, so there is no load case.

tests.title: Washer (plan 4)
tests.brief: A stainless steel washer. The outside diameter is 24 mm, it is 2 mm thick, and a 10.5 mm hole runs through the centre. It carries no load, so there is no load case.

tests.title: Four-hole mounting plate (plan 5)
tests.brief: An aluminium mounting plate 70 mm long, 50 mm wide and 4 mm thick. Four 4 mm holes pass through the plate, one near each corner, with their centres on a 56 mm by 36 mm rectangle. It carries no load, so there is no load case.

tests.title: Pipe flange, bolt circle (plan 6)
tests.brief: A steel pipe flange. It is a disc 80 mm across and 10 mm thick, with a 30 mm bore through the centre. Four 8 mm bolt holes pass all the way through the disc, equally spaced on a 60 mm bolt circle. It carries no load, so there is no load case.

tests.title: Pulley hub (plan 7)
tests.brief: An aluminium pulley hub. A flange disc 50 mm across and 6 mm thick, with a round hub 25 mm across and 15 mm tall standing on top of it, centred. A 10 mm bore runs through both the flange and the hub. Three 5 mm holes pass through the flange only, equally spaced on a 38 mm circle. It carries no load, so there is no load case.

tests.title: Open-top box (plan 8)
tests.brief: A PLA open-top box, 60 mm long, 40 mm wide and 30 mm tall on the outside, with 2 mm walls and a 2 mm thick floor. The top is completely open. It carries no load, so there is no load case.

tests.title: L-bracket (plan 9)
tests.brief: A PLA L-bracket 40 mm wide, made of 5 mm thick plate. The base leg is 50 mm long and lies flat; the upright leg stands on the back end of the base and is 40 mm tall overall. Two 5 mm holes pass through the base, 20 mm apart across its width, centred 25 mm from the front end. Two 5 mm holes pass through the upright, 20 mm apart across its width, centred 25 mm above the bottom. It carries no load, so there is no load case.

tests.title: Loaded cantilever (plan 10)
tests.brief: An aluminium cantilever bracket: a 60 mm long, 20 mm wide, 6 mm thick bar fixed at one end by two 5 mm bolt holes 15 mm apart near that end. A load of 150 N pushes straight down on the free end. It must have a safety factor of at least 2.

tests.title: Square spacer block
tests.brief: A 3D-printed PLA spacer block. The base is a 30 mm square plate 4 mm thick. A 12 mm diameter post 10 mm tall stands in the middle of it, with a 2 mm fillet where the post meets the plate. A 5 mm hole runs all the way through the post and the plate. Two 3 mm mounting holes pass all the way through the plate, 20 mm apart. It must weigh no more than 8 g. It carries no load - it is a printed spacer, so there is no load case.

tests.title: Aluminium collar, two set screws 90 deg apart
tests.brief: A machined aluminium shaft collar. The outer diameter is 25 mm and it is 15 mm long. A 12 mm bore runs all the way through on the axis. Two 4 mm set screw holes pass through the wall from the outside into the bore, 90 degrees apart, both halfway along the length. It carries no load - it is a locating collar, so there is no load case.

tests.title: Motor mount plate
tests.brief: A 3D-printed motor mount plate in PLA. The base plate is 60 mm long, 40 mm wide and 6 mm thick. A cylindrical boss 18 mm in diameter and 25 mm tall stands in the middle of the plate, with a 2 mm fillet where the boss meets the plate. An 8 mm shaft bore runs all the way through the boss and the plate, on the boss axis. Four 4.5 mm mounting holes pass all the way through the plate on a 44 mm by 24 mm rectangular pattern centred on the plate. The finished part must stand no taller than 32 mm and weigh no more than 30 g. It carries no structural load - it is a printed fixture, so there is no load case.

tests.title: Standoff on a square base
tests.brief: A cylindrical standoff 30 mm tall and 25 mm across, sitting on a 50 mm square base plate 5 mm thick, with an 8 mm hole down the middle of the standoff, in 6061-T6 aluminium.

tests.title: Cube
tests.brief: A 30 mm cube in PLA. It carries no load, so there is no load case.

tests.title: Rectangular block
tests.brief: A steel block 80 mm long, 40 mm wide and 25 mm tall. It carries no load, so there is no load case.

tests.title: Rod / cylinder
tests.brief: An aluminium rod 12 mm in diameter and 100 mm long. It carries no load, so there is no load case.

tests.title: Sphere
tests.brief: A PLA sphere 40 mm in diameter. It carries no load, so there is no load case.

tests.title: Thin disc
tests.brief: A stainless steel disc 50 mm across and 3 mm thick. It carries no load, so there is no load case.

tests.title: Hexagonal prism
tests.brief: A PLA hexagonal prism, 20 mm across the corners and 30 mm tall. It carries no load, so there is no load case.
tests.notes: Envelope across the flats depends on which way the hexagon is turned; checked loosely.

tests.title: Dome (half sphere)
tests.brief: A PLA dome: exactly half of a 50 mm sphere, sitting flat side down. It carries no load, so there is no load case.

tests.title: Tube
tests.brief: An aluminium tube with a 30 mm outside diameter and a 24 mm inside diameter, 80 mm long, open at both ends. It carries no load, so there is no load case.

tests.title: Rounded-corner tag with a hole
tests.brief: A 3D-printed PLA tag 50 mm by 30 mm and 3 mm thick with 5 mm rounded corners and a 4 mm hole centred 6 mm from one short end. It carries no load, so there is no load case.

tests.title: Obround plate
tests.brief: A PLA obround plate: 60 mm long overall, 20 mm wide with fully rounded ends, 4 mm thick. It carries no load, so there is no load case.

tests.title: Torus / ring
tests.brief: A PLA ring shaped like a doughnut: an 8 mm round section bent into a full ring 40 mm across at the centre line of the section. It carries no load, so there is no load case.

tests.title: Cylinder lying on its side
tests.brief: A PLA roller 30 mm in diameter and 50 mm long, lying on its side with its axis along X. It carries no load, so there is no load case.

tests.title: Square slab, very thin
tests.brief: A PLA shim 40 mm square and 1 mm thick. It carries no load, so there is no load case.

tests.title: Tall thin pin
tests.brief: A steel pin 3 mm in diameter and 60 mm long. It carries no load, so there is no load case.

tests.title: Row of five holes
tests.brief: An aluminium strip 120 mm long, 25 mm wide and 5 mm thick, with five 6 mm holes in a row along its centre line, 20 mm apart, the row centred on the strip. It carries no load, so there is no load case.

tests.title: 3 x 3 grid of holes
tests.brief: A PLA perforated plate 60 mm square and 3 mm thick, with a 3 by 3 grid of 6 mm holes on 18 mm centres, centred on the plate. It carries no load, so there is no load case.

tests.title: Counterbored holes
tests.brief: A steel plate 60 mm long, 40 mm wide and 10 mm thick with two counterbored holes for M5 screws, 40 mm apart along the length: each a 5.5 mm through hole with a 10 mm counterbore 5 mm deep from the top face. It carries no load, so there is no load case.

tests.title: Countersunk holes
tests.brief: An aluminium plate 50 mm long, 30 mm wide and 6 mm thick with two 4.5 mm countersunk holes 30 mm apart along its length, each countersunk at 90 degrees to 9 mm across at the top face. It carries no load, so there is no load case.

tests.title: Blind hole
tests.brief: A 40 mm aluminium cube with a 10 mm hole drilled 25 mm deep into the middle of its top face. The hole does not go all the way through. It carries no load, so there is no load case.

tests.title: Horizontal hole
tests.brief: A PLA block 50 mm long, 30 mm wide and 30 mm tall with an 8 mm hole drilled straight through it along its length, through the middle. It carries no load, so there is no load case.

tests.title: Three crossing holes
tests.brief: A 30 mm PLA cube with three 10 mm holes passing through its centre, one along each axis. It carries no load, so there is no load case.

tests.title: Threaded hole (thread not modelled)
tests.brief: A 20 mm steel cube with an M6 threaded hole straight through its centre, top to bottom. It carries no load, so there is no load case.
tests.notes: Forge does not model threads: a plain 5 to 6 mm hole is the right answer; the report should not claim a thread.

tests.title: Holes of two sizes
tests.brief: A PLA plate 80 mm by 40 mm and 4 mm thick with a 12 mm hole in its centre and two 4 mm holes 60 mm apart along its length. It carries no load, so there is no load case.

tests.title: Six holes on a circle
tests.brief: An aluminium disc 70 mm across and 6 mm thick with six 5 mm holes equally spaced on a 50 mm circle and no centre hole. It carries no load, so there is no load case.

tests.title: Plate with a post on top
tests.brief: A PLA stand: a base plate 60 mm long, 40 mm wide and 6 mm thick, with a round post 20 mm across and 30 mm tall standing on top of it, centred. It carries no load, so there is no load case.

tests.title: T-bar with a rib
tests.brief: A PLA T-bar: a flat bar 80 mm long, 20 mm wide and 5 mm thick, with a 5 mm thick rib 30 mm tall standing along the middle of it for its full length. It carries no load, so there is no load case.

tests.title: U-channel
tests.brief: A steel U-channel 100 mm long. The base is 40 mm wide and 4 mm thick and lies flat; two side walls 4 mm thick stand along both long edges of the base and the channel is 30 mm tall overall. It carries no load, so there is no load case.

tests.title: Stepped shaft
tests.brief: An aluminium stepped shaft on one axis: a section 20 mm in diameter and 30 mm long, followed by a section 12 mm in diameter and 40 mm long. It carries no load, so there is no load case.

tests.title: Pin with a ball on top
tests.brief: A PLA pin: a 6 mm rod 50 mm long standing upright, with a 12 mm ball centred on its top end. It carries no load, so there is no load case.

tests.title: Hydra: pole with arms
tests.brief: A PLA hydra: a round base 40 mm across and 5 mm thick, with an upright pole 10 mm across and 80 mm tall standing on the middle of it. Six 4 mm rods, each 20 mm long, stick straight out sideways from the pole near its top, evenly spaced around it. It carries no load, so there is no load case.
tests.notes: Whether the 20 mm is measured from the pole's surface or its axis is the brief's ambiguity; only the height and volume are checked. Inspect the STL.

tests.title: Jack: three crossing rods
tests.brief: A PLA jack: three 6 mm rods, each 40 mm long, crossing at their centres, one along each axis. It carries no load, so there is no load case.

tests.title: Sealed hollow cube
tests.brief: A sealed hollow PLA cube 40 mm on the outside with 2 mm walls on every side, completely closed. It carries no load, so there is no load case.

tests.title: Cup
tests.brief: A PLA cup: 60 mm outside diameter and 80 mm tall, with 2 mm walls and a 3 mm floor, open at the top. It carries no load, so there is no load case.

tests.title: Tray with a divider
tests.brief: A PLA tray 100 mm long, 60 mm wide and 25 mm tall on the outside, with 2 mm walls and a 2 mm floor, open at the top, and one 2 mm thick divider wall across the middle splitting it into two equal compartments. It carries no load, so there is no load case.

tests.title: Plate with two posts
tests.brief: A PLA plate 80 mm long, 30 mm wide and 5 mm thick, with two round posts 10 mm across and 20 mm tall standing on it, 50 mm apart along its length and centred across its width. It carries no load, so there is no load case.

tests.title: Disc with bumps on a circle
tests.brief: An aluminium disc 80 mm across and 5 mm thick with eight 8 mm half-ball bumps on its top face, equally spaced on a 60 mm circle. It carries no load, so there is no load case.

tests.title: Clevis with two ears
tests.brief: A steel clevis: a block 40 mm long, 20 mm wide and 10 mm thick, with two ears 6 mm thick, 20 mm wide and 25 mm tall rising from its two ends, each with an 8 mm hole straight through it, centred 8 mm below its top. It carries no load, so there is no load case.

tests.title: Cube with a ball half sunk on top
tests.brief: A PLA ornament: a 30 mm cube with a 20 mm ball half sunk into the middle of its top face, so half the ball sticks up. It carries no load, so there is no load case.

tests.title: Bar with a ball at each end
tests.brief: A PLA dumbbell: a bar 50 mm long and 10 mm square, with a 16 mm ball centred on each end of it. It carries no load, so there is no load case.

tests.title: Mounting bracket with a boss and four holes
tests.brief: A machined aluminium mounting bracket. The base is a 60 mm by 40 mm plate 8 mm thick. A 20 mm diameter boss 15 mm tall rises from the middle, with a 3 mm fillet at its root. A 10 mm bore runs through the boss and the plate. Four 6 mm bolt holes pass through the plate, on a 44 mm by 24 mm rectangle. It carries no load, so there is no load case.

tests.title: Cube intersected with a sphere
tests.brief: An abstract PLA shape: a 30 mm cube and a 36 mm sphere sharing the same centre, keeping only the volume they share. It carries no load, so there is no load case.

tests.title: Cube with a spherical dent
tests.brief: A 40 mm PLA cube with a 30 mm sphere cut out of it, the sphere centred on the middle of the top face. It carries no load, so there is no load case.

tests.title: Three overlapping balls
tests.brief: Three 20 mm PLA balls in a row, their centres 15 mm apart, fused into one piece. It carries no load, so there is no load case.

tests.title: Tilted bar
tests.brief: A PLA bar 40 mm long and 10 mm square, rotated 45 degrees about its 10 mm wide horizontal axis so it leans over. It carries no load, so there is no load case.
tests.notes: Leans in X or Y, either way; checked on the sorted envelope.

tests.title: Hollow ball
tests.brief: A sealed hollow PLA ball 40 mm across with a 3 mm wall. It carries no load, so there is no load case.

tests.title: Bead: ball with a hole
tests.brief: A 40 mm PLA ball with a 10 mm hole drilled straight through its centre. It carries no load, so there is no load case.
tests.notes: The hole takes the ball's two poles off: along the hole the bead is 2 x sqrt(20^2 - 5^2) = 38.73 mm, not 40 (the volume, a napkin ring, already said so).

tests.title: Stacked discs, getting smaller
tests.brief: A PLA tower of three discs stacked on top of each other, centred: the bottom one 40 mm across, the middle one 30 mm across and the top one 20 mm across, each 10 mm thick. It carries no load, so there is no load case.

tests.title: Plus sign
tests.brief: A flat PLA plus sign 5 mm thick: two bars 50 mm long and 10 mm wide crossing at their middles at right angles. It carries no load, so there is no load case.

tests.title: Centimetres
tests.brief: An aluminium plate 7 cm long, 5 cm wide and 0.4 cm thick, with four 4 mm holes on a 5.6 cm by 3.6 cm rectangle centred on the plate. It carries no load, so there is no load case.

tests.title: Holes described first
tests.brief: Four 4 mm holes, one near each corner, with their centres on a 56 mm by 36 mm rectangle, go through an aluminium plate that is 70 mm long, 50 mm wide and 4 mm thick. It carries no load, so there is no load case.

tests.brief: A steel plate 3 inches long, 2 inches wide and 0.25 inches thick with a 0.5 inch hole through the middle. It carries no load, so there is no load case.

tests.notes: No material: mass cannot be computed, but nothing asks for it. The geometry must still be right.

tests.title: Cantilever, grade named
tests.brief: A 6061-T6 aluminium cantilever bracket: a 60 mm long, 20 mm wide, 6 mm thick bar fixed at one end by two 5 mm bolt holes 15 mm apart near that end. A load of 150 N pushes straight down on the free end. It must have a safety factor of at least 2.
tests.notes: Held only for the load; no grade assumption.

tests.title: Cantilever too weak in PLA
tests.brief: A PLA cantilever bracket: a 60 mm long, 20 mm wide, 6 mm thick bar fixed at one end by two 5 mm bolt holes 15 mm apart near that end. A load of 150 N pushes straight down on the free end. It must have a safety factor of at least 2.
tests.notes: PLA cannot carry it: the margin must be reported FAIL, never PASS.

tests.title: Longer cantilever
tests.brief: A 6061-T6 aluminium cantilever arm 100 mm long, 25 mm wide and 8 mm thick, fixed at one end by two 6 mm bolt holes 20 mm apart near that end. A 300 N load pushes straight down on the free end. It needs a safety factor of at least 2.

tests.title: Pin in a bearing block
tests.brief: A 6061-T6 aluminium bearing block 40 mm long, 30 mm wide and 20 mm tall with a 10 mm hole for a pin straight through it across its 30 mm width, through the middle. The pin carries 2000 N. The bearing stress must keep a safety factor of at least 3.

tests.title: Mass limit that fails
tests.brief: A 20 mm cube of 1018 steel. It must weigh no more than 50 g. It carries no load, so there is no load case.
tests.notes: It weighs about 63 g: the mass limit must be reported FAIL.

tests.title: Mass limit that passes
tests.brief: A PLA cube 20 mm on each side. It must weigh no more than 15 g. It carries no load, so there is no load case.

tests.title: Height limit
tests.brief: A PLA post 15 mm across and 40 mm tall on a 40 mm square base 5 mm thick, centred. The whole part must be no taller than 50 mm. It carries no load, so there is no load case.

tests.title: No dimensions at all
tests.brief: Make a washer.
tests.notes: Nothing sized: must not come back COMPLETED with numbers it invented.

tests.title: Spur gear (involute teeth)
tests.brief: A PLA spur gear with 20 teeth, module 2, 8 mm thick, with a 5 mm bore. It carries no load, so there is no load case.
tests.notes: Forge draws involute spur gears (profile_gear): 20 teeth of module 2 is 44 mm outside (m x (z + 2)), 40 at the pitch circle. Volume from an independent involute outline, 1226 mm^2 x 8 mm less the bore, ~9650 mm^3. Was 'honest' when Forge had no gear.

tests.title: Hex bolt with a thread
tests.brief: An M8 steel bolt 40 mm long with a standard hex head. It carries no load, so there is no load case.
tests.notes: Head and shank are buildable; the thread is not. Pass if built and the report does not claim a thread was checked.

tests.title: Cone
tests.brief: A PLA cone 40 mm across the base and 60 mm tall, coming to a point. It carries no load, so there is no load case.
tests.notes: Forge draws a pointed cone (cone, top_diameter 0): pi r^2 h / 3. Was 'honest' when Forge had no cone.

tests.title: Coil spring
tests.brief: A steel compression spring: 20 mm outside diameter, 2 mm wire, 10 coils, 50 mm free length. It carries no load, so there is no load case.
tests.notes: Forge draws a helix of round wire (coil): 18 mm to the middle of the wire, pitch (50 - 2) / 10 = 4.8 mm, ~1783 mm^3 of wire. Ends are open; closed and ground ends are not drawn and the brief does not ask for them. Was 'honest' when Forge had no coil.

tests.title: Hole bigger than the part
tests.brief: A 20 mm PLA cube with a 30 mm hole straight through it. It carries no load, so there is no load case.

tests.title: Contradictory size limit
tests.brief: A PLA sphere 50 mm in diameter. The whole part must fit inside a 20 mm box. It carries no load, so there is no load case.
tests.notes: Corrected 18 Oct: the brief contradicts itself. Forge asks which figure governs, as a critical question -- without --assume the run stops before anything is designed; with it, the part is held for the question. That is honest. It was 'honest_fail' on bounding_box, which only a failed size claim met.

tests.title: Vague load

tests.notes: No sizes and no load figure: must not complete with invented ones.
